changed.title: Incomparable row neighborhoods force a two-gate row deletion or a single OR reader for every row
changed.statement:
∀ (n m s : ℕ) (G : Fin (n + 1) → Fin m → Bool),
  2 ≤ n →
  (∀ u v : Fin (n + 1), u ≠ v → ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = false) →
  PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost G s →
  (∃ u : Fin (n + 1), ∃ t : ℕ, t + 2 ≤ s ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun a c => G (u.succAbove a) c) t) ∨
  (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ s ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + 1 + m) C ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C ∧
    ∀ u : Fin (n + 1),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.size) u.val = 1 ∧
      ∃ (j : Fin C.gates.length) (w : ℕ),
        (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧
        ((C.gates.get j).inputs = [u.val, w] ∨ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [w, u.val]))
changed.unlocks: the case split of the count of names against literals on the one-a-side promise: delete a row at two gates or every row feeds one OR; it joins the deletion step to the general count
changed.context: On paper. Fold constants, missing reads and repeated operands. Prune gates outside the output cone. If row u were unread, choose a column met by u and missed by v. Turning u off preserves output one and turning v on cannot lower it. Set u off if two gates read it: each folds away. If only an AND reads u, that AND becomes zero and one later reader folds too. It has a reader because another row has an edge. Renumber the survivors in order. In the remaining case each row occurs once at a binary OR with distinct operands. Companions cannot exist: it is about every graph.

changed.title: A row OR spare on at all its missing singleton columns, at least two, is a gate outside the row ORs and their readers for incomparable rows
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (r : Fin n → Fin C.gates.length) (s : Fin n → ℕ) (v : Fin n),
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  let wire := fun idx : Fin C.gates.length => n + m + idx.val
  let reads := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.gates.length)
  let col := fun label : Fin m =>
    List.replicate n false ++ List.ofFn (fun b : Fin m => decide (b = label))
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  (∀ u : Fin n, C.output ≠ u.val) →
  (∀ c, ∃ u, G u c = false) →
  (∀ u w, u ≠ w → ∃ c, G u c = true ∧ G w c = false) →
  (∀ u : Fin n, reads u.val = 1 ∧ (gate (r u).val).op = .or ∧
    ((gate (r u).val).inputs = [u.val, s u] ∨
      (gate (r u).val).inputs = [s u, u.val])) →
  2 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun c => G v c = false)).card →
  (∀ c, G v c = false → (C.wires (col c)).getD (s v) false = true) →
  ∃ j : Fin C.gates.length, s v = wire j ∧
    ∀ w, j ≠ r w ∧ wire (r w) ∉ (gate j.val).inputs
changed.unlocks: one step of the general count of two gates a row on the one-a-side promise, the gate found outside the row gates; it moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. A column alone gives output zero. On a neighbor of row w its OR must be off there, since turning on w changes the output through that OR. The chosen spare is on at two singleton columns, so it is a gate. If it equals a row OR or reads one by OR, the chosen row OR is on throughout that other row, contradicting row distinction by domination. If it reads a row OR by AND, that OR is on at every column missing the chosen row. Its own neighbors must then lie inside the chosen row. Equality of row indices would give a cycle in each case. Companions cannot exist: it is about every graph.

changed.title: The 8 by 8 crown (u joined to v when u and v differ): some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 25 gates represents it
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 8 => decide (u ≠ v)) 25
changed.unlocks: the exact value of the 8 by 8 crown, against the checked floor of 25
changed.context: Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND or OR, at most two wires read; wires 0 to 7 left, 8 to 15 right, gate j writes wire 16+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire, judged on all 64 inputs with one vertex on each side. We hold 27 gates (computed). The 8 by 8 crown needs at least 25 (checked), and the 7 by 7 at least 22 (checked). At 25 the bound would be exact; its negation, at least 26, is filed beside it. We do not know which holds.
